args: Analyze the bounds validation in `frame_get_lazychunk` and its use by `frame_decompress_chunk` in `c-blosc2/blosc/frame.c`. What are the exact types/semantics of frame->len, header_len, chunk offsets, and cbytes in both contiguous-memory and file-backed branches, and what overflow-safe validation should be added so a returned lazy chunk always lies fully inside the actual contiguous frame buffer? Note any existing project conventions/error returns that should be followed.

The supplied ASan report shows an OOB 4-byte read in blosc_d after frame_decompress_chunk passes an attacker-forged cbytes to blosc2_decompress_ctx. The stated root cause is that the in-memory contiguous branch of frame_get_lazychunk checks only header_len + offset + BLOSC_MIN_HEADER_LENGTH against frame->len, reads cbytes from that minimum header, but does not ensure the full declared chunk is within frame->cframe. I have not edited code yet. I want to patch c-blosc2/blosc/frame.c at the root with subtraction-based bounds checks that account for signedness and arithmetic overflow while preserving file-backed behavior.
